headline: Another tanker struck a naval mine and caught fire east of the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday morning

sources: Iran's Army Navy / IRGC Navy statement, via Al Jazeera liveblog, Arab News, APA; UKMTO advisory 202-26 (Suspicious Activity)
fault_line: Mines as blockade enforcement or as an indiscriminate hazard -- who laid them, who clears them, and who pays when a nameless tanker burns?

sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- cause and fire] Iran's Army Navy said on Wednesday that an oil tanker caught fire after striking a naval mine in a mined/restricted area in the east of the Strait of Hormuz: 'Early this morning, a violating oil tanker caught fire after striking a naval mine in an unsafe, prohibited area in the east of the Strait of Hormuz.' IRGC Navy separately: 'the tanker struck a mine while passing through the mined and restricted eastern section... causing a fire. Passage through the Strait of Hormuz is possible in coordination with Iran.' Vessel NOT named; flag, owner, cargo, crew condition all unknown. [CONFIRMED -- the incident] UKMTO advisory 202-26 confirms it received a report of an incident involving a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz; crew status, damage extent and environmental impact unknown. UKMTO does NOT confirm a mine or a fire. [SCOPE -- the incident, not the cause] The UKMTO 202-26 incident itself was recorded at 0800-01; the mine/fire cause claim is the new element in this record. [TALLY UPDATE -- in-window] 10 attacks on ships in/near Hormuz recorded so far in November (Washington Institute for Near East Policy data via Reuters/CNA, CNA updated 13:25 ), after 37 in October -- the highest monthly total since the war began. [DO NOT MERGE] This Wednesday incident is distinct from Tuesday's three IRGC-claimed mine tankers (recorded 0200-01/0800-01) and from the Fujairah Energy projectile strike (1400-01).
sections.what_verified: 4 distinct tiered families: UKMTO (T1, incident confirmed, cause not stated), Al Jazeera (T2, STATE QA, carries the army statement), Arab News (T3), Gulf News (T3). APA and IRNA carry the same IRGC statement but have NO declared tier and do not count.
sections.what_disputed: UKMTO's own advisory mentions no mine and no fire. No independent party has confirmed the cause, the vessel's identity, or that it is burning. The US military recently claimed all mines had been cleared from the waterway. IRGC statements have previously described 'unauthorised route' incidents without naming vessels, and Tuesday's three-tanker claim also remains vessel-unidentified.
sections.why_matters: A fourth tanker in two days -- this time Iran's army says it hit a mine on Wednesday morning, and the official maritime watchdog will only confirm that something happened.
sections.context: Background: IN-WINDOW (AJ liveblog 07:20 GMT = 11:20 ; APA 11:04 ; in the 11:00-12:00 window, missed by the 12:00 scan which recorded UKMTO 202-26 only as 'no follow-up') -- Iran's army/IRGC Navy: another tanker struck a naval mine and caught fire east of the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday morning

totw_analysis: Our read: A fourth tanker in two days -- this time Iran's army says it hit a mine on Wednesday morning, and the official maritime watchdog will only confirm that something happened. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Mines as blockade enforcement or as an indiscriminate hazard -- who laid them, who clears them, and who pays when a nameless tanker burns?
